dae_X10_034.context_nosym: This system models the bending behavior of an Euler-Bernoulli beam subjected to distributed loads and potential discontinuities (springs or supports). The coupled differential equations solve the fourth-order beam bending problem using an auxiliary beam method to handle discontinuities from rotational and translational springs, integrating load distributions with generalized functions (Heaviside step functions) to determine deflection throughout the beam.

dae_X10_037.context_nosym: This system models the evaporation and spreading dynamics of a marine oil spill, specifically tracking the evolution of thick and thin slick components on the ocean surface. dae_X10_038.context_nosym: This system models magnetohydrodynamic (MHD) turbulence in the solar wind, treating it as a natural turbulence laboratory where plasma flows interact with magnetic fields. Given turbulence transfer functions, forcing terms, and spectral energy distributions as inputs, the model computes the evolution of Elsässer variables (describing plasma velocity and magnetic field fluctuations), energy dissipation rates, plasma density, and spectral characteristics across different wavenumber scales. The coupled equations describe turbulent energy cascade, Hall-MHD magnetic field evolution, and compressible MHD effects that together characterize how turbulent energy flows from large to small scales and is ultimately dissipated as heat in the solar wind plasma.

dae_X3_080.context_nosym: This scenario models the adjoint stability analysis of a linear dynamical system, where given the system matrix, a weighting matrix, and state information, the adjoint vector is computed by solving the backward-in-time adjoint equation to assess system optimality or stability. The computation determines the transformation matrix that maps the input vector to the state vector, along with the adjoint eigenvectors that provide modal decomposition of the system response using a biorthogonal representation with the forward eigenvectors. These coupled equations enable sensitivity analysis and optimal control design by relating the forward system dynamics to their adjoint counterparts through spectral decomposition.

dae_X3_083.context_nosym: This scenario models a heat exchanger system where an internal fluid flows through a tube and exchanges heat with an external medium. dae_X8_007.context_nosym: This model simulates the coupled hydrodynamic, thermal, and ecological dynamics of a stratified lake system to predict harmful cyanobacteria blooms during summer heatwaves.
